sheet.no_analysis: No analysis yet. Run “michel analyze --project {name}” to complete these details.
fact.direct: your project asks for it directly
decision.title: Your decision
decision.why_needed: Required to ignore: say in one sentence why this does not concern you.
decision.will.fix: Michel will note that you plan to fix this vulnerability. It will no longer show as waiting.
decision.will.defer: Michel will set this vulnerability aside until {date}. He will bring it back then. He will do it sooner if it changes.
decision.will.ignore: Michel will ignore this vulnerability with your reason. He will bring it back only if it changes.
decision.done.fix: Noted: you will fix this vulnerability.
decision.proof_hint: You can find it with “michel audit list”.
decision.gone: Michel no longer sees this vulnerability. If it comes back, he will ask you again only if something changed.
decision.failed: Michel could not save your decision.
decision.why_required: Write why you ignore this vulnerability.
decision.why_too_long: Your reason is longer than 1,000 characters. Shorten it.
decision.until_past: Pick a date from tomorrow on.
decision.until_invalid: Michel does not understand this date.
decision.until_not_defer: A date is only used to put a vulnerability off. Remove it, or pick Put off.
decision.action_unknown: Pick Fix, Put off or Ignore.
settings.title: Settings
settings.token_saved: A token is saved in this browser.
settings.token_missing: No token is saved in this browser.
auth.title: Michel needs your access token
auth.body: Run “michel serve”, then open the link it shows.
auth.why: The token keeps other programs on your computer from reading your vulnerabilities.
auth.rejected: Michel does not recognize this token. Check that you copied all of it, or open the link again.
offline.title: Michel is not answering
offline.hint: Run “michel serve” in a terminal, then reload this page.

error.generic: Michel could not read this page's data.
nav.label: Pages
exploited.hint: Attackers already use them. Deal with them first.

exploited.decided.one: {n} exploited vulnerability you put off or ignored.
exploited.decided.other: {n} exploited vulnerabilities you put off or ignored.
reading.title: To read
reading.hint: News about the technologies you use.
reading.failed: Michel could not mark it as read.
catalog.title: Catalog
fact.epss_value: {p} chance of an attack within 30 days: more than for {pct} of the flaws.
sources.title: Your sources
sources.updating: Michel is reading your sources. It can take a few minutes.
sources.update_failed.one: {n} source could not be read: its line says why.
sources.update_failed.other: {n} sources could not be read: their lines say why.
sources.kind_hint.osv: The vulnerability databases Michel checks your dependencies against, offline.
sources.kind_hint.enrichment: Lists that tell which flaws are exploited, or likely to be.
sources.kind_hint.feed: Security news about the technologies you use.
sources.kind_hint.plugin: Analysis tools whose reports Michel reads.
sources.kind_hint.skill: Instructions for your AI assistant, copied into your skills folder.
sources.kind_hint.mcp: Tools for your AI assistant. Michel shows you how to add them; he never runs them.
sources.last.waiting_consent: {ago} · not read: it waits for your consent
sources.done.hidden: Source hidden. Show the hidden sources, then Reset, to bring it back.
sources.done.reset: Source set back as in Michel's catalog.
sources.remove_confirm.title: Uninstall {name}?
sources.remove_confirm.body: This source is installed on this computer. Removing it uninstalls it: Michel deletes the folder he installed, and only that one.
consent.title: Michel needs your consent
consent.will_write: Michel will write this line in your policy file:
consent.why: Without this line, Michel contacts no site. Turning the source off keeps it; “michel source disable --forget” removes it.
install.title: Install {name}
install.loading: Michel is downloading this version to show it to you. Nothing is installed yet.
install.license_unknown: No licence found: check the terms before you use it.
install.trust.user: Added by you: not in Michel's catalog.
install.trust.archived: Archived by its author: no longer maintained.
install.head: Start of its instructions
install.never_run: Michel never runs anything from this repository.
install.replaces: It replaces {old}, which Michel will delete.
install.mcp_nothing: Michel writes nothing in your Claude Code settings. To add this server, run:
install.mcp_no_launch: Michel does not know how to start this server: read its page.
install.mcp_downloads: This command downloads code when it starts, out of Michel's control.
install.same_files: Same files as the installed version.
add.title: Add a source
add.kind_hint: Tell Michel what it is: he asks only for what it needs.
add.name: Name
add.name_hint: Shown in the lists; the key is made from it.
add.url_hint: The feed or page Michel will read. Only secure (https) addresses.
add.format_hint_feed: Leave “auto”: Michel recognizes RSS and Atom. “page” watches a page for changes; “github_advisories” reads the advisories of a GitHub repository.
add.format_hint_plugin: The format of the report the tool writes.
add.repo_hint: Where the skill or server lives, for example example/skill.
add.repo_hint_feed: Only with the format github_advisories: Michel reads the advisories of this repository.
add.path_hint: Optional: the folder of the skill, when the repository holds several.
add.pin_hint: Michel installs exactly this version, and never a newer one without asking you.
add.ecosystem_hint: The name of the OSV database, for example PyPI. Michel downloads it to check your dependencies offline.
add.tool_hint: The program that writes the report; “generic” for any SARIF tool.
add.input_hint: Optional: the report Michel reads when you run the plugin. Michel only reads it.
add.tech_hint: For example nginx, postgresql: the items about them go to “To read”.
add.done: Added. It stays off until you turn it on.
run.title: Run {name}
run.running: {name} is running. You can leave this page: the findings will join the others.
discover.title: To discover
discover.hint: Repositories found on GitHub by topic. Nothing is added without you.
today.fixes.title: Fixes to review
today.fixes.hint: Michel and the agent prepared these fixes on a copy. Nothing changes in your projects until you approve them.
fix.title: Fix
fix.intro: Pick a flaw in the list. An agent prepares the fix on a copy of your project; nothing changes on your side until you approve it.
fix.empty: Nothing to fix for now: no open flaw, no fix in progress.
fix.pick: Pick a flaw in the list to start.
fix.line.preparing: The agent is working on it.
fix.line.proposed: A fix is waiting for your approval.
fix.line.approved: Approved: Michel is creating the branch.
fix.line.inconclusive: Branch created: Michel will check at the next scan that the flaw is gone.
fix.line.failed: The last attempt did not succeed. You can try again.
fix.agent.not_ready: Claude Code is not ready on this computer
fix.agent.unknown: Michel could not check Claude Code. Try again in a moment.
fix.chat.label: Conversation with the agent
fix.chat.start_hint: An agent (Claude Code) prepares the fix on a copy of your project. You will read its proposal before anything changes. You can also write to it below.
fix.chat.starting: Michel is preparing a copy of your project and starting the agent. This can take a few minutes.
fix.chat.empty: The conversation starts as soon as the agent gets to work.
fix.chat.proposed: The proposal is ready: read it, then approve or refuse it.
fix.chat.applied: Branch {branch} is ready in your repository. Merge it when you like, then deploy as usual.
fix.chat.placeholder: Write to the agent, for example: “keep the current version”
fix.chat.closed: The agent is done: you can no longer write to it here.
fix.chat.reconnecting: The connection to Michel dropped; trying again…
fix.secret_hint: Michel hid this secret key (password, access token…) before showing the code to the agent. The real value stays in your project.
fix.flaw.title: The flaw
fix.flaw.loading: Michel is opening the flaw's sheet.
fix.proposal.title: The proposal
fix.proposal.sites.one: {n} place in your code uses it
fix.proposal.sites.other: {n} places in your code use it
fix.proposal.no_sites: your code does not use it directly
fix.proposal.tests_not_run: the tests could not be run
fix.proposal.none: No proposal yet: the agent is working on it.
fix.proposal.rescan_clean: Michel scanned the copy again: the flaw is gone.
fix.proposal.rescan_dirty: Michel scanned the copy again: the flaw is still there.
fix.proposal.tests_not_run_hint: The tests could not run on the copy: check yourself that your site works before you merge the branch.
fix.proposal.tests_failed_hint: Some tests fail with this fix: read the details before you approve.
fix.proposal.risk: Estimated risk: {risk} out of 100 (the lower, the safer)
fix.proposal.updated: The agent replaced its proposal: here is the new one.
fix.proposal.approve_hint: Approving creates a michel/fix-… branch in your repository. Your current branch and your files stay as they are.
fix.proposal.approving: Michel is creating the branch in your repository…
fix.refuse.title: Refuse this proposal?
fix.refuse.body: Nothing will be applied. The flaw stays to fix: you can start a new fix later.
fix.done.proven: Michel checked: the flaw is gone from your project.
fix.done.inconclusive: Branch {branch} exists, but Michel could not check yet that the flaw is gone. Merge the branch: Michel will check at the next scan.
fix.done.approved: You approved this fix. Michel could not create the branch yet; it will try again the next time Michel starts.
fix.done.refused: You refused this proposal: nothing was applied.
fix.done.failed: This attempt did not succeed: nothing was applied.
fix.done.superseded: A newer attempt replaced this one.
fix.consent.title: Let an agent work on {project}?
fixset.title: Fix settings
fixset.loading: Michel is reading the project's settings.
fixset.auto: Apply safe minor updates on my behalf
fixset.auto_hint: Counts only at the “Apply what I allowed” level. Then Michel creates the branch without waiting for your approval, but only if the fix only touches the project's list of libraries, without a big version jump (for example from 7 to 8), if the tests pass and if the flaw is gone at the new scan.
fixset.ai_given: You gave your consent on {date}: an agent can work on this project.
fixset.ai_missing: No consent yet. Michel asks you the first time you click “Fix”.
fixset.ai_levels: Without your AI consent, no agent works on this project: Michel explains the flaws, that's all.
fix.level.0.title: Report
fix.level.0.text: Michel tells you about the flaws in your digest and on the page, nothing more.
fix.level.1.title: Explain
fix.level.1.text: Michel explains each flaw; you can ask an agent to prepare a fix with “Fix” (with your AI consent).
fix.level.2.title: Prepare
fix.level.2.text: An agent prepares a fix on its own for each flaw that allows it; it waits for your approval.
fix.level.3.title: Apply what I allowed
fix.level.3.text: Like “Prepare”, and Michel creates the branch on its own for the fixes that follow your rules; the others wait for your approval.
fix.activity.propose: The agent sends its proposal: Michel runs the tests on the copy.
fix.consent.strict_intro: Your policy is in strict_local mode: nothing leaves your computer and no external AI is used. It is the strongest protection.
fix.consent.strict_change: For an agent (Claude Code) to fix this project, Michel must switch your policy to standard mode. You lose the guarantee that nothing leaves your computer: external AI may be used. You keep a precise frame: only towards the addresses listed below, and only for the projects you consent to. Michel keeps a copy of the old policy (.bak file), so you can go back.
fix.consent.strict_accept: Switch to standard mode and allow external AI
fixset.ai_strict: Your policy is in strict_local mode: no external AI. For an agent to work on this project, Michel must first switch to standard mode, with your consent.
fix.proposal.commands: What Michel ran on the copy
fix.proposal.cmd.tests: Your project's tests (the test command you set)
servers.level.0.title: Report
servers.level.0.text: Michel tells you and fills in the server's sheet, without preparing anything.
servers.level.1.title: Explain, and prepare on request
servers.level.1.text: Michel explains each flaw; he prepares the scripts when you click "Fix".
servers.level.2.title: Prepare
servers.level.2.text: Michel prepares the scripts for each flaw on his own; they wait for your approval.
servers.level.3.title: Apply what I allowed
servers.level.3.text: Like "Prepare", and Michel runs on his own the fixes that keep all your rules.
servers.state.unread: No known flaw, but Michel could not see everything.
servers.state.key_unconfirmed: Not checked yet: confirm the server's fingerprint first.
servers.state.checking: Michel is checking this server now.
servers.state.inactive: Michel no longer checks this server.
servers.state.check_failed: The last check did not complete.
servers.finding.php_version_unknown: Michel could not read the PHP version of this server.
servers.finding.php_version_unknown_hint: Without the version, Michel cannot tell whether PHP has a known flaw. Check that php -v works for the SSH user, then check again.
servers.step.done.undo: done, the server is as it was
servers.step.result.rolled_back: failed after the change, the script put the files back
servers.step.result.rollback_bad: failed, and putting the files back failed too
servers.step.result.pkg_failed: the upgrade failed, the package may have changed
servers.step.result.stderr: PHP reported an error while reading the file
servers.step.result.no_site_check: Michel cannot check the site from this computer
servers.step.result.partial: the check could not judge everything
servers.step.result.unknown: no answer (time limit reached or connection lost)
servers.line.proposed: A fix waits for your approval.
servers.line.snapshot: A fix waits for your snapshot, then your approval.
servers.line.approved_user: Approved: run the script yourself, then tell Michel.
servers.line.approved_auto: Approved automatically by your rules, not run yet.
servers.line.running: The script is running on the server.
servers.line.unknown: Michel cannot tell what the script changed: check the server.
servers.line.applied: The script ran: Michel is checking the server.
servers.line.inconclusive: The script ran, but Michel could not prove the fix.
servers.line.failed: The last attempt did not succeed. You can prepare another one.
servers.backup.kept: {file}: copy kept on your computer, encrypted.
servers.backup.key_lost: {file}: key lost. The copy on your computer can no longer be opened; the one on the server stays.
servers.backup.damaged: {file}: does not match. The copy on your computer was damaged; the one on the server stays.
servers.title: Servers
servers.intro: Michel reads your servers over SSH, without installing or changing anything there, and tells you whether they have a known flaw.
servers.empty: Michel does not watch any server yet.
servers.empty_hint: Click "Find my servers": Michel reads your SSH configuration and the PhpStorm settings of your projects, then you tick the ones to add.
servers.discover.title: Find my servers
servers.discover.loading: Michel is reading your SSH configuration and your PhpStorm projects.
servers.discover.none: Michel found no new server in your SSH configuration or in your projects.
servers.discover.none_hint: Add it by hand: you need its address, the SSH user and the port.
servers.discover.authorize: Adding this server allows Michel to connect to it.
servers.discover.authorize_more: Michel writes a network rule for it in your policy file (SSH and, if you give the site's address, the site itself). He takes it back when you remove the server.
servers.discover.name: Name (for you)
servers.discover.key_only: Michel connects only with a key of your SSH agent, never with a password. Tip: a separate SSH user for Michel, with its own key.
servers.hostkey.title: Fingerprint of {name}
servers.hostkey.loading: Michel is reading the fingerprint the server shows.
servers.hostkey.first: The server shows this fingerprint. Compare it with the one your host gives (or, on the server: ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub). If it is the same, confirm it: Michel will then connect only if the server shows this key.
servers.hostkey.pinned: This fingerprint is already confirmed: Michel connects to this server only.
servers.hostkey.changed: Warning: the server shows a fingerprint other than the one you confirmed.
servers.hostkey.changed_why: It may be an attack: someone is pretending to be your server. It may also come from a reinstall. Michel did not connect and changed nothing. Check with your host before replacing the fingerprint.
servers.hostkey.replace_ok: I know why the key changed (for example, I reinstalled the server) and I checked the new fingerprint with my host.
servers.sheet.loading: Michel is opening the server's sheet.
servers.sheet.checking: Michel is checking the server… this can take a minute.
servers.sheet.source: To judge the system packages, Michel needs the source {key}, turned off for now. Turn it on in the Sources page.
servers.sheet.no_flaws: No known flaw on this server.
servers.sheet.no_flaws_unchecked: Michel has not checked this server yet: he knows nothing of its flaws.
servers.sheet.mitigation: reduces the risk, does not fix
servers.sheet.fix_report_only: This server is set to "Report": change its level in the settings for Michel to prepare a fix.
servers.sheet.no_projects: No project linked to this server.
servers.sheet.unseen_none: Michel could read everything at the last check.
servers.sheet.unseen_hint: Michel never forces a refused read: if it matters, give the SSH user read rights, then check again.
servers.sheet.backups.one: Michel keeps {n} file copy of this server ({size}), encrypted, on your computer, for 90 days.
servers.sheet.backups.other: Michel keeps {n} file copies of this server ({size}), encrypted, on your computer, for 90 days.
servers.sheet.backups_server: On the server, the copies stay in /var/lib/michel/backups/ and ~/.michel/backups/: Michel never deletes them. Empty these folders yourself when you no longer need them.
servers.settings.title: Settings
servers.settings.level: What Michel does with the flaws
servers.settings.auto: Fix the known risky settings on his own (level 3)
servers.settings.auto_hint: Only PHP settings planned by Michel's rules, never a package upgrade nor an agent proposal. Michel first tests the configuration, tries on the preprod if there is one, then checks the site. Works only if Michel runs the scripts himself.
servers.settings.executor.user: You: Michel prepares the scripts, you run them on the server yourself.
servers.settings.executor.michel: Michel: after your approval, Michel runs the script over SSH and follows each step.
servers.settings.sudo.none: Michel never uses sudo on this server.
servers.settings.sudo.nopasswd: Michel may run a fix script with sudo -n (sudo without a password), never to read.
servers.settings.site_sentence: After each fix, Michel opens {url} from your computer to check that the site answers.
servers.settings.site_none: Without an address, Michel cannot check the site after a fix, nor prove that it worked.
servers.settings.preprod_sentence: Fixes are first tried on {name}; production is only offered after a full success there.
servers.settings.preprod_empty: No preprod: fixes are made directly here.
servers.settings.hds_note: An HDS server holds health data: Michel never sends an AI agent there, and prepares only his own fixes.
servers.ai.title: AI agent for this server
servers.ai.of_preprod: The agent receives the inventory of the preprod {name}: the consent below is about it.
servers.ai.given: Consent given on {date}: the agent may read the masked versions and settings of {name}.
servers.ai.missing: No consent: Michel prepares his fixes alone. He calls on the agent only for the cases to study.
servers.ai.give: See what leaves and give consent
servers.ai.revoked: Consent withdrawn: no agent works on this server any more.
servers.unknown.title: An earlier fix was left without an answer
servers.unknown.body: On this server, a script stopped without Michel knowing what it changed. Before preparing another fix, check the server yourself, then mark that fix as checked.
servers.remove.title: Remove {name} from Michel?
servers.remove.body: Nothing is done on the server. Michel forgets its sheet and takes back the network rules he wrote for it; the file copies already made stay on the server.
servers.remove.rules_not_removed: The server is removed, but Michel could not take its network rules out of the policy file. Remove them by hand (in network.allow, the target.ssh and target.http entries).
srvfix.for_production: This fix is first tried on the preprod, before the production {name}.
srvfix.mitigation: Reduces the risk, does not fix: this setting closes a way in, but the flaw stays open until PHP is upgraded.
srvfix.snapshot.title: First: a snapshot
srvfix.snapshot.body: Make a snapshot of this server at your host. A package upgrade has no undo script: your snapshot is the only way back.
srvfix.approve_hint.michel: Approve: Michel sends exactly this script over SSH and follows each step. If the site stops answering, he undoes it at once.
srvfix.approve_hint.user: Approve: Michel gives you the script to run on the server yourself. He does not connect to apply it.
srvfix.approve_snapshot_first: Tick "Snapshot done" first to be able to approve.
srvfix.approving: Michel is running the script on the server…
srvfix.copy_failed: The browser could not copy: select the text and copy it yourself.
srvfix.rollback.config: The script itself puts the kept files back and reloads PHP if a step fails after the change. Later, the "Undo" script puts the server back as it was.
srvfix.rollback.package: No script can undo a package upgrade: the way back is your snapshot.
srvfix.user.title: Your turn to run the script
srvfix.user.body: Copy the "Apply" script, run it on the server, then click "I applied it": Michel then checks the site and the server. Keep the "Undo" script at hand.
srvfix.user.root: This script must be run as root: otherwise it stops before changing anything.
srvfix.applying: Michel is checking the site and the server…
srvfix.auto: Approved automatically by your rules, not run yet: Michel runs it as soon as he can reach the server.
srvfix.approved: Approved: Michel is running the script.
srvfix.running: The script is running on the server. Each step shows here.
srvfix.unknown.title: Michel cannot tell what the script changed
srvfix.unknown.body: The script did not answer in time, or the connection dropped. Michel guessed nothing and undid nothing. Look at the server yourself (the changed file, PHP, the site). When done, tell Michel: he closes this fix and you can prepare another one.
srvfix.restore.title: Restore your snapshot now
srvfix.restore.body: The package upgrade went wrong and no script can undo it. Restore the snapshot you made at your host, then check the server.
srvfix.backup_hint: To put a file back by hand: copy the kept file over the changed file (cp copy file), then reload PHP.
srvfix.done.proven_fixed: Fixed: the new check no longer sees the problem.
srvfix.done.inconclusive: The script ran, but Michel could not prove the fix.
srvfix.done.refused: You refused this proposal: nothing was run on the server.
srvfix.done.superseded: A newer fix replaced this one.
srvfix.no_agent_chat: Michel prepares this fix alone, from his rules: no agent, nothing to discuss.
projsrv.title: Servers of this project
projsrv.none: No server linked to this project. On the Servers page, "Find my servers" reads the project's PhpStorm settings.
today.servers.title: Affected servers
today.servers.hint: A known flaw affects these servers: their sheet says what to do.
srvfix.rolled_back: Rollback done: the server is as it was before the fix.
servers.headline.urgent_one: The server {name} has an urgent flaw.
servers.headline.critical_one: The server {name} has a critical flaw.
servers.headline.word_one: Open its sheet: it says what to do first.
servers.headline.word_many: Open their sheets: they say what to do first.
servers.level.3.warn: Note: a fix Michel prepared, even on your request, can then run on its own when it keeps these rules.
fix.intro_server: For a server, Michel prepares the scripts from his own rules, without an agent; nothing changes on the server without your approval.
srvfix.scripts_unreadable: Michel cannot show these scripts as they are (unreadable text). Run nothing: prepare a new fix.
